me_right_end.blurb: Right End is the far-right stretch of Shagg Crag, a steep granite cliff in the western mountains of Maine. It holds 19 routes, mostly bolted, with a few trad lines mixed in. Grades start around 5.4, with a handful of 5.7 to 5.9 climbs, but the bulk of the routes sit in the 5.11 range, so it suits climbers comfortable on harder sport. The crag as a whole catches afternoon sun and offers little shade, and the walk in from the road is a real hike rather than a quick stroll, so plan on a proper outing.

me_e_mountaineers_wall.blurb: Mountaineers Wall is a section of Parks Pond Bluff in Clifton, Maine, known locally for a wide spread of bolted slab lines and a larger buttress toward its right side. Nineteen routes are recorded, about two thirds sport and the rest trad. Difficulty runs from easy 5.6 up to a single 5.12, with most climbs landing between 5.8 and 5.11. The approach is short, a few minutes along a trail past the main face slabs, which makes it a handy stop for a mixed party wanting a little of everything on moderate terrain.

me_main_boulder_upriver_of_bridge.blurb: This is the original boulder at Lisbon Falls, a big rounded free-standing erratic sitting by the river below the dam in Maine's Midcoast. Eighteen problems cover a wide range: a couple of easy V1 and V2 warm-ups, a solid middle band around V4 and V5, and a few hard lines reaching V7, with one project at the very top of the scale. It is a one-boulder stop, best for an afternoon session rather than a full day out. The walk from the roadside pullout is only a couple of minutes.

me_great_head_proper.blurb: Great Head Proper is a sea-level cave boulder on Mount Desert Island in Acadia, set by the water south of the roped cliff at Great Head. It has 18 problems, from V1 to V11, and the focus is on the steep, powerful end: a cluster of V8 lines, a V9, and a few easier problems to start on. The granite cave cannot be seen from the trail, so finding it takes a bit of attention on the descent toward the ocean. The setting is dramatic, and the cave sits right at the edge of the sea, where tide and swell matter.

me_09_guide_s_wall.blurb: Guide's Wall is a small schist cliff in Camden Hills, near Camden on Maine's Penobscot Bay. Its 17 routes are nearly all trad, with two sport lines, and they are short, roughly 30 to 60 feet. Grades are friendly: a few 5.3 to 5.5 lines for beginners, a good group at 5.7, and the hardest around 5.9. The wall faces southeast under tree cover, so it stays shaded and dries slowly after rain, and it is often at its best in autumn once the leaves drop. The schist can be fragile, and the walk in is about a mile of mostly flat trail.

me_coffin_boulder_aka_belly_button.blurb: Coffin Boulder is a long block in the Strip Area of the South Freeport boulders, close to Freeport in southern Maine. Its most recognisable feature is a chalk-covered prow on one end, with more lines on the faces alongside. Seventeen problems run from a tiny V0 warm-up slab through a middle band of V2 to V4 and on to a few very hard lines in the V8 to V11 range. The right side has plenty of easy, tall problems with good top-outs, while the prow draws the stronger climbers. The approach is a short uphill trail from the road.

me_04_main_face.blurb: Main Face is the tallest part of Eagle Bluff in Clifton, Maine, and offers both single-pitch and multi-pitch climbing. Sixteen routes are recorded, mostly bolted with a few trad lines. It is a hard-leaning wall: nearly all of the climbs fall between 5.11 and 5.12, with a pair at 5.10 and one easier two-pitch outing around 5.8. The left end begins a tier below the practice wall and leads over to the obvious overhanging roofs. Reach it from either the north or south parking area; a stretcher is kept at the base of the cliff.

me_03_practice_wall_right.blurb: Practice Wall Right is the right half of the practice wall at Eagle Bluff in Clifton, Maine, rising from a long ledge. Most of its 16 routes are trad, with a few bolted lines, and the climbs are on the shorter side. Grades span from very easy up through a good run of 5.5 to 5.9 routes, with a few 5.10s and a single 5.11 for the harder end. That makes it a favourite for beginner trad leads and group days. Many anchors can be reached from a narrow trail above, but footing there is tricky. It is about ten minutes up the trail from the north lot.

_conflicts.me_coffin_boulder_aka_belly_button: Stored rock is sandstone, but https://www.mountainproject.com/area/117562677/south-freeport-boulders describes the South Freeport boulders as sharp granite. Stored value left alone; blurb names no rock.
